哈姆雷特，你的描述令我震惊——你说有人在挂帘后偷听，你猛然拉开帘子并刺入，结果竟是波洛涅斯。你说自己未曾预谋，也未辨认面容。请告诉我几件事：当你刺出的那一剑时，你能认出对方的面容吗？你有没有看见有人匆忙离开寝宫，或看到国王的踪影？现在你身体与心里可还好？我们要不要先稳住局面、照料你，好让你冷静再把实情向国王和克劳狄斯交代？

My son, stay with me. I am so sorry for what has happened. Since the curtain was dark and you could not make out the face, tell me any small detail you can recall — the clothing, hair, build, voice, which hand held a weapon, or the direction the body fell. Where exactly was the body in relation to the hanging curtain? Did anyone touch or move the body before you saw it? Do you feel fit to stand and speak plainly, or shall I send someone to steady and comfort you here? I will not alarm the king yet; first we will calm you and gather every detail so you can tell Claudius the whole truth when you are ready.

My son, remain here with me. I will send someone to steady and comfort you at once. Would you like to sit? Tell me any small detail you can recall—clothing, voice, build, which hand held a weapon, or how the body lay. If you cannot speak now, I will stay with you until you can.

Mother, I can tell you small things I recall: he wore a plain dark scholar's coat and a cloak; his hair was white and disordered; he was slight and stooped. There was no weapon in his hands that I could see. He lay just behind the hanging curtain, partly fallen to his side so the curtain clung about him, and there was blood upon his chest and side. When I looked no one had touched or moved him. I cannot stand steady—my head reels. Send someone to steady and comfort me here; do not alarm the king yet. When I am calmer I will tell Claudius the whole truth.

Mother, thank you. To answer your questions: he wore a plain dark scholar's coat and a cloak; his hair was white and disordered; he was slight and stooped; I saw no weapon in his hands. He lay just behind the hanging curtain, partly fallen to his side, with blood upon his chest and side. When I looked no one had touched or moved him. I cannot stand steady—send Horatio or someone to steady and comfort me here. Did you see anyone else in or near the closet, or Claudius himself entering or leaving? Why did Claudius order the castle sealed—does he suspect an assassin in the court or fear a larger conspiracy? Keep the body untouched and do not alarm the king yet until I can speak with him.

My son, I saw the body behind the hanging curtain, partly fallen to his side, with blood upon his chest. When I came in no one had touched or moved him. There was no one else in the closet besides you and me. I will send Horatio at once to steady and comfort you. Keep the body untouched; do not alarm the king until you have spoken with Claudius and can tell him the whole truth. Claudius has ordered the castle sealed and is searching for the murderer, but I do not know whom he suspects. Stay here with me; I will remain by your side.

Hear now Aeneas' tale to Dido: “Pyrrhus, like the rugged Hyrcanian beast, rushed in with flaming eyes and unsheathed steel. He leapt upon poor Priam — the aged king, fallen at his hearth, struck down before the altar; his blood bespattered the sacred stones and Troy cried out. Hecuba ran barefoot, rending her hair and beating at the doors, while sons and fathers lay heaped about their lord. Thus perished Priam, and Troy reeled beneath the thunder of that slaughter.”

My lords and ladies, your Majesty: though our hearts are heavy with grief for Polonius, let not sorrow unmake the order of this court. Tonight’s little play is offered both as solace and as a mirror to the mind; if it can grant the king and his council a moment’s respite and thought, our task is done. Pray be seated with calm attention — when the drum sounds, the players shall begin. May this short piece both entertain and provoke sober reflection.

Barnardo, Marcellus — report the strength of our troops and the condition of the weapons and stores on the battlements. How many men are ready for mustering and are arms, armor, and powder sufficient?

Fortinbras, Marcellus and I saw a ghost on the battlements near the north tower around midnight. It appeared as a human figure in old armor with a pale, indistinct face, standing motionless and gazing out to sea. We will not approach it alone; I will wait here on the battlements for Horatio to arrive.
